title: Variables and built-in functions
test_conventions: Tests are Python assert snippets executed AFTER the learner's code, in the same namespace, one snippet at a time. Everything the learner's code printed is available to tests as the string variable __stdout__, and the learner's source code is available as the string __source__ (some hidden tests re-run that source with different input values to make sure the result is computed, not typed). expected_output comparisons are exact after stripping trailing whitespace on each line (and trailing blank lines). tests[].visible defaults to true; visible:false tests are hidden and always carry a failure_message. For fill_blank, blanks in starter_code are written ___ and are filled in order; every alternative in blanks[].answer must pass the tests. For parsons, lines are shown shuffled; correct_order lists, for each position of the solution, the index into lines; distractors are extra lines that must not be used. For predict, expected_output must be one of choices; for debug with expected_output the fixed program's stdout must match it exactly.

blocks.concept_tr: Değişkenler: isim etiketi ve yeniden atama

worked_example.code:
score = 10
score = score + 5
bonus = score
score = 0
print(score, bonus)
notes: Assignment evaluates the right side first and then attaches the name on the left to the result, so score = score + 5 uses the old score (10) and moves the tag to 15.
bonus = score attaches a second tag to the same value 15; it does not create a link between the two names.
score = 0 moves only the score tag, so bonus still shows 15 and the program prints 0 15.
notes_tr: Atama önce sağ tarafı hesaplar, sonra soldaki ismi sonuca bağlar; bu yüzden score = score + 5 eski score'u (10) kullanır ve etiketi 15'e taşır.
bonus = score aynı 15 değerine ikinci bir etiket takar; iki isim arasında bir bağ kurmaz.
score = 0 yalnızca score etiketini taşır; bonus hâlâ 15'i gösterir ve program 0 15 yazdırır.

exercises.model_answer: A variable is a name tag on an object. b = a puts a second tag on the same object, 10. a = 20 moves only the a tag to a new object, 20; the b tag stays on 10 because there is no link between the names.

blocks.concept_tr: İsimlendirme kuralları, snake_case ve yerleşik isimler

worked_example.code:
first_name = 'Elif'
last_name = 'Yılmaz'
full_name = first_name + ' ' + last_name
total = 120 + 80
print(full_name, total)
notes: Names use letters, digits and underscores, start with a letter or underscore, and are case-sensitive.
Python style is snake_case: lowercase words joined by underscores, such as first_name and full_name.
The sum is called total, not sum, because sum is a built-in function and reusing its name would break later calls to sum().
notes_tr: İsimler harf, rakam ve alt çizgi içerir, harf ya da alt çizgiyle başlar ve büyük-küçük harfe duyarlıdır.
Python stili snake_case'tir: alt çizgiyle birleşen küçük harfli kelimeler, örneğin first_name ve full_name.
Toplamın adı sum değil total'dır, çünkü sum yerleşik bir fonksiyondur ve adını yeniden kullanmak sonraki sum() çağrılarını bozar.

notes: Values from input() or a form are always strings, so int() or float() must turn them into numbers before you calculate.
